text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- President Thomas Klestil has returned to hospital after lung problems resurfaced. Doctors said they were alarmed by Klestil's condition during his first television appearance last week after he spent almost two months in hospital to cure an acute bout of pneumonia.
- Direct insurers have not yet had a great impact on the Austrian market, even though their premiums are about 40 percent below the market's average.
- Austrian border police to patrol the Slovak border by helicopter.
- Canadian-Austrian car parts maker Magna to invest one billion schillings in Graz, southern Austria, to supply Eurostar car plant, a joint venture between Chrysler and Steyr.
- Postal savings bank PSK should be allowed to make loans to private customers, Finance Minister Viktor Klima says.
- Carinthian spin-edge technology group SEZ's newly issued shares are in strong demand.
- Chancellor Franz Vranitzky says Austrian troops may take part in the multinational peace force for Zaire.
- The new city government for Vienna, a coalition of Social Democrats and the conservative People's Party, is bogged down by personnel discussions.
- Far-right leader Joerg Haider says the federal trade union congress OeGB is taxed too lightly.
- Chief executive of steel maker Boehler-Uddeholm, Claus Raidl, says Vienna's stock exchange is unlikely to survive the introduction of Europe's planned single currency.
- Salomon Brothers says shares of oil and chemicals group OMV, Austria's largest industrial conglomerate, are undervalued.
- President Klestil to decide next spring whether he will seek another term in office when his current term expires 1998.
